cultural.vision_reason: This is a strip-woven man's gown (boubou/riga) with embroidered chest panel, a classic West African garment style worn across Wolof and neighboring groups in Senegal; plausible for the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga). The body is formed of 126 uniform narrow strips, hand-woven from hand-spun cotton and silk, sewn together along the selvedges. Each strip has in the warp two broad stripes of magenta (alaari) silk separated by thin lines of white, yellow and indigo cotton, and edged on the sides with thin lines of yellow and indigo; the weft is of indigo, which gives the silk a purple tinge.The strips have been hand-sewn together such that the stitching is almost invisible. The strips forming the body of the gown have been sewn vertically, but folded towards the upper half to narrow the strip; the folding opens gradually lower down the sides of the body of the gown so that its skirt flares outwards. The sleeves are sewn horizontally. At the front is added a large pocket. The pocket, shoulder and front are hand-embroidered in green thread with the ‘eight knives’ (aska takwas) pattern in satin stitch and buttonhole eyelet stitch. Along the inside at the bottom of the gown is a lining of white cotton and alaari silk.
